issues.legal_issue: A factual defense raised for the first time in a special-leave appeal cannot be entertained when it is inconsistent with the pleadings and would prejudice the opposing party by depriving them of an opportunity to rebut it.
material_facts: The tenants had pleaded that the tenant remained in possession of the entire shop, but first argued in the special-leave petition that his sons occupied a portion exclusively with his permission.
The permission argument had not been raised in the written statement or pressed before the lower authorities.
The landlord had no opportunity to contest the new factual claim.
issues.conclusion: The tenants were not permitted to raise the new factual plea in the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: A new plea of fact, unlike a plea of law, should not be entertained when it was not pleaded or pursued below, is inconsistent with the existing case, and the opposing party had no opportunity to rebut it. No earlier cases or specific statutory provisions are cited for this principle.

rule.if: special_leave_appeal and new_factual_plea and inconsistent_with_earlier_pleading and not raised_below and opposing_party_lacked_opportunity_to_rebut

predicates.special_leave_appeal: The case is a special-leave appeal.
predicates.new_factual_plea: A party advances a factual defense that was not part of its earlier case.
predicates.inconsistent_with_earlier_pleading: The new factual defense conflicts with the party's earlier pleading.
predicates.raised_below: The party raised the factual defense before the lower decision-makers.
predicates.opposing_party_lacked_opportunity_to_reb: The opposing party had no opportunity to contest the new factual defense.

issues.definition: When a party in a special-leave appeal advances a new factual defense inconsistent with its earlier pleading, did not raise it below, and deprived the opponent of an opportunity to rebut it, the defense is not entertained.

issues.legal_issue: Family relationship and shared household arrangements alone do not establish that family members permissively possess a portion of rented premises.
material_facts: The tenant was the father of the two family members occupying the divided portion of the shop.
The tenants relied on the father-son relationship to support their claim that the sons occupied that portion with permission.
The record also referred to joint living and joint messing, but the permission claim had not been pleaded below.
issues.conclusion: No presumption of permissive possession could be drawn merely from the family relationship or from joint living and joint messing.
issues.legal_principle: The court stated that a father-son relationship, joint living, or joint messing alone does not give rise to a presumption that the sons were in permissive possession of the premises. No earlier cases or specific statutory provisions are cited for this principle.

predicates.rent_control_ejectment_appeal: The case is an appeal in an ejectment proceeding concerning rented premises.
predicates.family_relationship_and_shared_household: The occupants are related to the tenant and live or share meals together.
predicates.no_independent_basis_for_permission: There is no basis for inferring permission apart from the relationship and shared household arrangements.

issues.definition: In a rent-control ejectment appeal, a family relationship and shared household arrangements, without an independent basis for permission, do not establish permissive possession.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant parts with possession of a portion of rented premises when that portion is divided off and is exclusively occupied by other persons carrying on a separate business, rather than by the tenant as part of a joint business.
material_facts: The shop was divided by a wooden partition into two portions with separate doors and no direct passage between them.
The tenant occupied one portion as a clinic, while his sons occupied the other portion and conducted a motor-car business there.
Each portion was locked separately, and the sons were found to have exclusive possession of their portion.
The claim that the motor-car business was a joint business was rejected; the tenant had not reported income from it and the business account books were not produced.
The lower authorities' findings were confirmed, and the Supreme Court accepted that the tenant had parted with possession of the sons' portion.
issues.conclusion: The tenant had parted with possession of the portion exclusively occupied by the other occupants, and the ejectment ground under proviso (b) to Section 14(1) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, was established.
issues.legal_principle: Under proviso (b) to Section 14(1) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, the relevant ground is that the tenant has sublet, assigned, or otherwise parted with possession of the premises or a part of them. The court accepted the concurrent factual finding of exclusive possession and rejected the claim of joint business. No earlier cases are cited.

rule.if: rent_control_ejectment_for_parting_with_possession and premises_physically_divided and other_occupants_have_exclusive_possession_of_a_portion and tenant_uses_a_separate_portion and joint_business_claim_not_established

predicates.rent_control_ejectment_for_parting_with_: The proceeding seeks ejectment on the basis that the tenant has transferred or parted with possession of rented premises or part of them.
predicates.premises_physically_divided: The premises are divided into separate portions that do not allow direct passage between them.
predicates.other_occupants_have_exclusive_possessio: Persons other than the tenant exclusively occupy and separately secure one portion of the premises.
predicates.tenant_uses_a_separate_portion: The tenant continues to use a different portion of the premises for the tenant's own activity.
predicates.joint_business_claim_not_established: The claim that the tenant and the other occupants conduct a joint business from the premises is not proved.

issues.definition: Where rented premises in an ejectment proceeding are divided into separate portions, other occupants exclusively possess one portion, the tenant uses another, and a claimed joint business is not established, the tenant has parted with possession of a portion.
